question.problem: The irradiance $I,$ in $W/{m}^{2},$ of a lamp placed in the center of a spherical chamber varies inversely with the **square** of the radius $r$ of the spherical chamber, measured in meters. It is known that the irradiance is $0.6\,W/{m}^{2}$ when the radius of the chamber is $3\,m.$ What equation gives the relationship between $I$ and $r?$
question.worked_solution:
Since the irradiance $I$ is inversely proportional to the square of the radius of the spherical chamber, $r$, we must have

$$
I=\frac{k}{{r}^{2}},
$$

where $k$ is the constant of variation.

We are told that $I=0.6\,W/{m}^{2}$ when $r=3\,\text{m}.$ We can use this information to solve for $k,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}0.6 & =\frac{k}{{3}^{2}} \\ 0.6 & =\frac{k}{9} \\ 0.6\cdot 9 & =k \\ 5.4 & =k\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our inverse variation equation is

$$
I=\frac{5.4}{{r}^{2}}.
$$
